findings: BLOCKER — AC-9 is unfulfilled and the implementation violates ADR-0013. src/svg/reference/expand.c builds an expanded SVG buffer up to 16 MiB by copying source spans and rewriting <use> elements; src/svg/clip/clip.c copies clip-path child bytes into another generated SVG buffer, also with a 16 MiB cap. ADR-0013 permits only compile-time-bounded temporary buffers of at most 4 KiB containing generated syntax/constants, never copied or rewritten document bytes. Runtime caps and source-hash checks do not satisfy that rule.

src/svg/reference/expand.c also creates a source map whose allocation grows with generated output and can reach 1,048,576 entries. This conflicts with the work-order prohibition on allocations scaling with source/reference expansion, independently of the explicit buffer violation.

Gradient defaults are not SVG-spec-correct for userSpaceOnUse: gradient_coordinates uses numeric defaults such as linear x2=1 and radial cx/cy/r=0.5, and rejects coordinate percentages. SVG defaults are percentage-based and depend on the viewport. The implementation therefore does not meet the requirement to tie radial behavior and defaults to the cited specification.

The supplied tests do not demonstrate the full AC-2/AC-3 matrix: the shown tests check gradient direction and radial center-versus-edge behavior, but not exact endpoint/interpolation results, and the supplied diff shows no independent rsvg-convert differential fixtures or comparison evidence. The runner's exit summaries do not establish those omitted assertions.

AC-1 and command execution portion of AC-4 are supported by zero exits for Debug configure/build/CTest, sanitizers, Release configure/build and ./dev verify; however, the actual CTest count and claimed absence of skips/reports are not included. AC-2 through AC-8 are not fully substantiated by supplied material: focused matrix, differential comparison, fuzz case count/report, benchmark trials/metrics, corpus hashes/outcomes and path-guard evidence are not shown. Passing command exit summaries alone do not verify these evidence-specific criteria.
summary: Fail. The known AC-9 failure is a release blocker under ADR-0013, and the candidate contains source-copy-generated buffers that directly breach the ADR. Additional spec and evidence gaps remain.
